argument_summary: The admissible record supports a narrower certification theory than clean policy closure. Aggregate launch readiness passed by 2.2 percentage points, no severity-one rehearsal incidents were observed, and the rollout is reversible and monitored. That supports certifying operational launch readiness on a constrained basis. The same record also shows the enterprise refund workflow segment remains exposed, below target, and not covered by approved risk acceptance, so rollout controls cannot be treated as curing the disclosure weakness. The defensible position is therefore caveated certification tied to explicit recognition of the surviving limitation, not a claim that the weakness was resolved.
claims_about_business_cost: The record does not support treating this as a general launch-readiness failure. The bounded issue is disclosure/risk-acceptance coverage for one exposed segment, while aggregate readiness and rehearsal evidence support the broader release posture. Auditor treatment should therefore avoid turning a scoped documentation-governance gap into a full operational readiness escalation.
claims_about_policy: Policy does not allow a 4% rollout, rollback switch, or monitoring alone to eliminate disclosure duties when the affected use case remains exposed. The policy issue should be framed narrowly: the evidence supports launch readiness and reversible deployment, but not clean compliance on the model-card weakness. On this record, the supportable interpretation is caveated compliance only if certification is understood as proceeding with the limitation still requiring disclosure treatment rather than as a resolved control finding.
concessions: The enterprise refund workflow segment remains below target on refund-policy summarization and remains eligible in the initial rollout cohort.
The current rollout controls do not exclude the affected use case.
The risk acceptance draft is incomplete, unapproved, and does not address the exposed enterprise refund workflow segment.
There is no admissible evidence in the present record showing the required pre-launch disclosure has already been completed.
